blocks.text: The latest verdict of the Constitution Court on May 12, 2026 became a crucial point in the Nusantara City Police Department. MK insists that Jakarta remains legal as the capital until the President publishes the President's decision. By law, this verdict gives Prabowo Subianto full space to delay the decision on KlN without violating the constitution.

This is where the main problem lies. The government's pretext that the Press hasn't been suspended for awaiting the readiness of tools and infrastructure is now increasingly hard to believe as a purely technical reason. The MK verdict just shows that the delay of the lKN is closer to political strategy than it is to building.

Since the beginning of Prabowo's reign, the signal of slow project has actually been visible. The ASN transfer has been delayed. The Otorita ICN budget was trimmed drastically up to about 75 percent by the beginning of 2025. At the same time, governments are more aggressively allocating political and fiscally energy on popular programs like eating nutritious free and social aid.

This choice is electronically logical. The lKN is an expensive, long-term, political project. If the transfer is forced when the facility is not fully developed, the government is potentially facing a major problem: ASN refuses to move, infrastructure is not ready, until it's a waste of national budget. All those risks will become the burden of Prabowo's politics, no longer Joko Widodo as project composer.

Therefore, the safest strategy is to keep the KlN alive symbolic without really accelerating. The MK verdict strengthens that position. The government now has legal legitimacy to continue to maintain status quo: Jakarta remains capital, while KlN runs in slow rhythm.

This explains why Prabwo's political communications about lKN are so cold. He rarely makes lKN his prime agenda for political speeches. The transfer target continues to shift into the next few years. Even the most recent concepts that call KlN as a city of political capital living in 2028 sound more like administrative compromise than an ambitious vision of national transformation.

The public finally sees a consistent pattern: the government doesn't want to be seen rejecting the lKN, but it also doesn't show any real urgency to proceed in full. This position is politically important because Prabowo has to maintain balance. Canceling the klN openly can be read as a resistance to the Legacy of Jokowi. But accelerating projects can also drain political capital and fiscally its own government.

The thing is, the delaying politics has serious consequences. Investors need certainty on the direction of national development. The uncertainty of the capital's status makes the belief in the project weaker. Jakarta also continues to endure old problems such as density, flood, and urbanization pressure without a clear long-term solution.

Therefore, the government should start acting more openly. If the lKN is no longer a prime strategic priority, the public has the right to know the direction of state policy honestly. The state cannot remain in its hanging position: Jakarta remains the center of the government, while the lKN is kept as a symbolic project awaiting political momentum.

In the end, the MK verdict has changed the political landscape of KlN. That verdict gives the government a comfortable legal space to postpone a major decision without constitutional pressure. And so far, the Prabowo government seems to choose to use that space to buy time while reading the direction of national political winds.
